claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your situation.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children under 16 years old, or any children aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have a child. My son Alex is 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have a son named Alex who is 8 years old.

Now, to continue assessing your eligibility:

**Do you live with Alex in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me. He lives with his mum.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. So Alex lives with his mum rather than with you.

In this situation, you may still be able to get Child Benefit if you're making financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep. This could include things like food, clothes, pocket money, or contributions towards his accommodation.

**Are you currently making any financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep (such as maintenance payments, pocket money, or money towards food, clothes, or housing)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do help out with things for Alex. I contribute towards his clothes and things he needs for school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. You're making contributions towards Alex's clothes and school needs.

To properly assess your eligibility, I need to understand the level of your contributions:

**Are your contributions towards Alex's upkeep at least equal to the current Child Benefit payment amount (which is £24.50 per week for the first child)?** 

In other words, are you contributing at least £24.50 worth of support per week on average towards his clothes, school needs, and other upkeep?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, let me think... I help out when I can, but I'd say it's probably around £10 a week on average when I add it all up.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. So your contributions average around £10 per week towards Alex's upkeep.

Just to make sure I have the complete picture, I need to ask one more question:

**Are you living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the rules for Child Benefit when a child lives with someone else, here's the situation:

You would normally get Child Benefit for 8 weeks after a child goes to live with someone else if nobody else claims. However, to continue receiving it beyond 8 weeks, you need to be making financial contributions towards the child's upkeep that are **at least equal to or greater than the Child Benefit payment amount**.

The current Child Benefit rate is £24.50 per week for the first child. Your contributions of approximately £10 per week fall short of this threshold.

This means:
- You could potentially receive Child Benefit for up to 8 weeks from when Alex went to live with his mum (if you haven't already received it for that period)
- After 8 weeks, without contributions meeting or exceeding £24.50 per week, you would not be eligible to continue receiving Child Benefit for Alex

Additionally, it's important to note that only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child. If Alex's mum is already receiving Child Benefit for him, you would not be able to claim it.
